news.title: Football Australia pleads for more time to digest Fifa’s controversial World Cup plans
news.lede: FA resists immediate criticism of privatisation push. More information requested to ‘properly assess’ implications. Football Australia has resisted immediate criticism of Fifa’s plan to seek private investment despite an international outcry, instead calling for more information about the controversial proposal. Football’s world governing body announced plans this week to sell a stake in the commercial rights to its tournaments, including the World Cup, to private investors, in a move led by the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino.

news.title: Infantino's greed has football on brink 60 years on from England's greatest day
news.lede: THE World Cup used to be so simple — and today serves as the perfect reminder of that. It was exactly 60 years ago that Bobby Moore was lifting the Jules Rimet trophy and being hoisted on the shoulders of his England team-mates. Those iconic scenes at Wembley came after a tournament that had just 16 teams and lasted only 20 days. There were no hydration breaks or half-time shows and certainly no private investors looking for a slice of the pie.

news.title: Fifa opens disciplinary proceedings against Argentina over Falklands banner and final chaos
news.lede: Players held banner after semi-final against England. Paredes and Molina investigated over brawl after final. Fifa has opened disciplinary ­proceedings against Argentina over the Falkland Islands banner ­displayed after their World Cup semi‑final win against England in Atlanta. As Argentina celebrated ­reaching the final with their dramatic 2-1 ­victory, several players held a sign ­proclaiming “Las Malvinas son ­Argentinas” – the ­Malvinas are Argentinian – in ­reference to the ­British overseas territory in the south Atlantic.

news.title: Infantino defends plan to sell World Cup stakes but could Uefa launch boycott?
news.lede: Fifa President Gianni Infantino called the plan to sell stakes in the World Cup a proposal but “not an obligation” after the idea provoked a furious response from football authorities. Fifa announced plans this week to create a $20 billion subsidiary to run the World Cup and its other events, ⁠and said it will offer stakes of up to ​20 per cent ⁠in it to ‌external investors. The proposal drew strong criticism from the ​sport's regional confederations, who said they were blindsided by the plan from the world governing body. But Infantino said strengthening the commercial side of the game is the natural next step in this evolution.

news.title: Bastian Schweinsteiger, Oliver Kahn weren’t pleased with Jamal Musiala’s lack of reaction at World Cup
news.lede: There is an old school way of thinking about and playing the game, which pins players and teams against each other. While maybe not going as far to designate the opposition as enemies, they certainly were not friends. That mentality is starting to slowly erode in modern sports as more players are exposed to each other at younger ages, which can create a bond or a friendship rather than a rivalry. It is hard to say, but Bastian Schweinsteiger and Oliver Kahn sound like they would like to see a little more fire from German players moving forward — including Bayern Munich star Jamal Musiala.

news.title: Football Australia breaks silence on FIFA boss’ $40m World Cup shakedown as civil war erupts
news.lede: Football Australia has broken its silence as governing bodies around the globe have shared their disbelief and outrage at being held to ransom over FIFA’s plans to sell a stake in the business operations of the World Cup and its other competitions to private investors. FIFA president Gianni Infantino plans to create a semi-private subsidiary called FIFA Forward Enterprise with FIFA holding a majority share, the 211 member nations having a 20 per cent share and 20 to 30 per cent stake sold off to private investors. news.title: Argentina Faces FIFA Sanctions Over Incidents at World Cup Final Match
news.lede: The FIFA Disciplinary Commission opened proceedings against the Argentine Football Association (AFA), footballers and technical staff. The world football governing body confirmed this Wednesday the opening of an expedited investigation evaluating potential violations of Articles 13, 14, 15, and 17 of the FIFA Disciplinary Code. The ruling covers the misuse of a sporting event for non-competition demonstrations, inappropriate conduct by delegations, expressions of discrimination, and racist aggressions. According to the official statement, the commission is also examining breaches related to order and security protocols during the tournament.

news.title: Argentina's Nicolás Tagliafico and Caro Calvagni escape to paradise after the World Cup
news.lede: After Argentina's World Cup run, Nicolás Tagliafico and his wife Caro Calvagni traded the pressure of football for a relaxing getaway in Greece. The couple shared stunning moments from their vacation, enjoying crystal-clear waters, breathtaking coastal views and the slower pace of the Greek islands as they recharge before the new club season begins. With preseason just around the corner, Tagliafico is making the most of his time off before returning to Lyon, while fans continue celebrating the defender's World Cup journey.
